claim: 17 potential target genes were selected which have been proven to play important roles in neural modulation.

evidence: Based on bioinformatic prediction and literature knowledge

claim: hsa-miR-30a-5p and hsa-miR-7-5p were involved in multiple regulation.
source: Target genes were predicted to be regulated by multiple miRNAs, among which hsa-miR-30a-5p and hsa-miR-7-5p were involved in multiple regulation.
evidence: Inferred from miRNA-mRNA regulatory network analysis

claim: Exosomes reduced the expression of downstream genes STAT3, CHUK, and PTPN1 in NSCs after OGD/R.
source: The results confirmed that exosomes reduced the expression of downstream genes in NSCs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B) as well as in brain tissues (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C, D), suggesting that exosomes might modulate the recipient cells and brain tissues through carrying miRNAs that regulate the expression of target genes.
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B

claim: Exosomes reduced the expression of downstream genes STAT3, CHUK, and PTPN1 in MCAO/R mice brain tissues.
source: The results confirmed that exosomes reduced the expression of downstream genes in NSCs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B) as well as in brain tissues (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C, D), suggesting that exosomes might modulate the recipient cells and brain tissues through carrying miRNAs that regulate the expression of target genes.
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C, D

claim: Exosomes might modulate the recipient cells and brain tissues through carrying miRNAs that regulate the expression of target genes.
source: The results confirmed that exosomes reduced the expression of downstream genes in NSCs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B) as well as in brain tissues (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C, D), suggesting that exosomes might modulate the recipient cells and brain tissues through carrying miRNAs that regulate the expression of target genes.
evidence: Inferred from reduced expression of predicted target genes with exosome treatment

claim: The predicted target genes of exosomal miRNAs were concentrated in functions and pathways that could regulate the cellular behavior of transplanted NSCs as well as the microenvironment remodeling.
source: Therefore, the predicted target genes of exosomal miRNAs were concentrated in the functions and pathways that could regulate the cellular behavior of transplanted NSCs as well as the microenvironment remodeling.
evidence: Inferred from GO and KEGG pathway enrichment analysis results

claim: NSC-derived exosomes might regulate the transplanted NSCs and the surrounding microenvironment through carrying miRNAs which could further modulate the downstream genes and pathways.
source: Taken together, our findings suggested that NSC-derived exosomes might regulate the transplanted NSCs and the surrounding microenvironment through carrying the miRNAs which could further modulate the downstream genes and pathways in both the NSCs and the surrounding cells (Figure 6).
evidence: Inferred from combined results of miRNA profiling, target gene prediction, and functional validation

claim: Poor survival and differentiation of grafted cells have limited the efficacy and application of stem cell-based therapy.
source: Stem cell-based therapy is an emerging and promising method to treat stroke, due to its effectiveness in cell replacement, neuroprotection, angiogenesis, and modulation of inflammation and immune response (Hao et al., 2014), but poor survival and differentiation of grafted cells have limited its efficacy and application (Jiang et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Jiang et al., 2019

claim: NSCs could effectively promote the recovery of motor function post-stroke in mice.
source: Consistent with previous reports (Wei et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2019), our results confirmed that NSCs could effectively promote the recovery of motor function post-stroke in mice.
evidence: Supported by citations to Wei et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2019 and confirmed by current study data

claim: Exosomes could promote the repairment of the damaged brain tissue as well as the functional recovery in MCAO/R mice.
source: Importantly, we demonstrated that exosomes could promote the repairment of the damaged brain tissue as well as the functional recovery, enhance the differentiation of the grafted NSCs in the infarct area, reduce the oxidative stress and inflammation, and alleviate the formation of glial scars in MCAO/R mice.
evidence: Supported by multiple experimental data from the current study

claim: Exosomes enhance the differentiation of the grafted NSCs in the infarct area.
source: Importantly, we demonstrated that exosomes could promote the repairment of the damaged brain tissue as well as the functional recovery, enhance the differentiation of the grafted NSCs in the infarct area, reduce the oxidative stress and inflammation, and alleviate the formation of glial scars in MCAO/R mice.
evidence: Supported by differentiation marker data from the current study

claim: Exosomes reduce the oxidative stress and inflammation in MCAO/R mice.
source: Importantly, we demonstrated that exosomes could promote the repairment of the damaged brain tissue as well as the functional recovery, enhance the differentiation of the grafted NSCs in the infarct area, reduce the oxidative stress and inflammation, and alleviate the formation of glial scars in MCAO/R mice.
evidence: Supported by ROS, MDA, and inflammatory cytokine data from the current study

claim: Exosomes alleviate the formation of glial scars in MCAO/R mice.
source: Importantly, we demonstrated that exosomes could promote the repairment of the damaged brain tissue as well as the functional recovery, enhance the differentiation of the grafted NSCs in the infarct area, reduce the oxidative stress and inflammation, and alleviate the formation of glial scars in MCAO/R mice.
evidence: Supported by GFAP staining data from the current study

claim: The pathological process of ischemia–reperfusion includes the generation of ROS, brain edema, and the increased levels of inflammation.
source: The pathological process of ischemia–reperfusion includes the generation of ROS, brain edema, and the increased levels of inflammation, which leads to the tough microenvironment for the transplanted stem cells to survive and differentiate (Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2019

claim: Transplantation of human hematopoietic stem cells triggers replication stress and induces increasing ROS levels in mice.
source: Yahata et al., 2011 found that transplantation of human hematopoietic stem cells triggers replication stress and induces increasing ROS levels in mice.
evidence: Supported by citation to Yahata et al., 2011

claim: Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells transplantation has been reported to increase oxidative stress levels in mouse muscle cells.
source: Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells transplantation has also been reported to increase oxidative stress levels in mouse muscle cells (Liu et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2019

claim: Chemokines released by macrophages and endothelial cells after stroke recruit peripheral immune cells to flood into the damaged brain.
source: Besides the oxidative stress, the chemokines released by macrophages and endothelial cells after stroke, such as chemokine group CXC ligand 1 (CXCL1), recruit peripheral immune cells to flood into the damaged brain, which causes immune-inflammatory damage (Ormstad et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ormstad et al., 2011

claim: Transplantation of exogenous stem cells could aggravate the inflammatory response around infract area due to the immune rejection.
source: Meanwhile, transplantation of exogenous stem cells could aggravate the inflammatory response around infract area due to the immune rejection (Hao et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hao et al., 2014

claim: ESC-derived exosomes decrease the inflammatory response, alleviate neuronal death, and improve long-term recovery after MCAO/R through increasing regulatory T cells.
source: Xia et al. reported that ESC-derived exosomes decrease the inflammatory response, alleviate neuronal death, and improve long-term recovery after MCAO/R through increasing regulatory T cells (Xia et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Xia et al., 2021

claim: NSC-derived exosomes have been demonstrated to improve a variety of neurological diseases, such as Alzheimer's disease, spinal cord injury, and ischemic stroke.
source: Due to the properties of regulating signaling pathways in target cells, and remodeling the microenvironment (Vogel et al., 2018), NSC-derived exosomes have been demonstrated to improve a variety of neurological diseases, such as Alzheimer's disease (Liu et al., 2020), spinal cord injury (Ma et al., 2019), and ischemic stroke (Sun et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Liu et al., 2020; Ma et al., 2019; Sun et al., 2019

claim: Exosomes promote the maturation of both neuron and glial cells in vitro.
source: Recent evidence demonstrated that exosomes promote the maturation of both neuron and glial cells in vitro (Yuan et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yuan et al., 2021

claim: Excessive initiation of apoptosis has been implicated in stroke.
source: Furthermore, excessive initiation of apoptosis has also been implicated in stroke (Hwang et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hwang et al., 2013

claim: NSC-derived exosomes could reduce the oxidative stress and the inflammatory response, and promote the differentiation of transplanted NSCs and reduce excessive apoptosis in the brain of MCAO/R mice.
source: Here, we showed that NSC-derived exosomes could reduce the oxidative stress and the inflammatory response, and promote the differentiation of transplanted NSCs and reduce excessive apoptosis in the brain of MCAO/R mice.
evidence: Supported by multiple experimental data from the current study

claim: Exosomes could promote the therapeutic effects of transplanted NSCs at multiple levels.
source: Therefore, our results indicated that exosomes could promote the therapeutic effects of transplanted NSCs at multiple levels.
evidence: Inferred from multiple beneficial effects observed with exosome treatment

claim: Stem cell-derived exosomes had neural protective effects and could promote recovery after ischemic stroke.
source: Previous studies have shown that stem cell-derived exosomes had neural protective effects and could promote recovery after ischemic stroke (Webb et al., 2018; Sun et al., 2019; Xia et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Webb et al., 2018; Sun et al., 2019; Xia et al., 2021

claim: The delivery of exosomes alone did not show significant neural protective effects in this study.
source: Although the delivery of exosomes alone used in this study did not show significant neural protective effects, it indeed ameliorated oxidative and inflammatory lesion conditions, promoted neuronal repairment, and potentiated the therapeutic power of transplanted NSCs, suggesting that the application of exosomes could be an effective adjuvant for NSC-based therapy.
evidence: Based on experimental results from the current study

claim: The application of exosomes could be an effective adjuvant for NSC-based therapy.
source: Although the delivery of exosomes alone used in this study did not show significant neural protective effects, it indeed ameliorated oxidative and inflammatory lesion conditions, promoted neuronal repairment, and potentiated the therapeutic power of transplanted NSCs, suggesting that the application of exosomes could be an effective adjuvant for NSC-based therapy.
evidence: Inferred from enhanced therapeutic effects when exosomes were combined with NSCs

claim: Exosomes are ideal carriers for drug delivery.
source: Besides, as exosomes are ideal carriers for drug delivery (Chen et al., 2021), modifications of exosomes by adding drugs or other functional molecules could potentially further enhance the beneficial effects of exosome treatment.
evidence: Supported by citation to Chen et al., 2021

claim: Modifications of exosomes by adding drugs or other functional molecules could potentially further enhance the beneficial effects of exosome treatment.
source: Besides, as exosomes are ideal carriers for drug delivery (Chen et al., 2021), modifications of exosomes by adding drugs or other functional molecules could potentially further enhance the beneficial effects of exosome treatment.
evidence: Speculative statement about potential future applications

claim: miRNAs were reported to be one of the major exosomal components.
source: As miRNAs were reported to be one of the major exosomal components, we profiled the miRNAs from NSC-derived exosomes to explore the molecular basis for the effects of exosomes as we observed in this study.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about exosome composition

claim: The predicted target genes of exosomal miRNAs were concentrated in the functions and pathways that could regulate the NSCs' behavior and the surrounding microenvironment.
source: Bioinformatic enrichment analysis in this study suggested that the predicted target genes of exosomal miRNAs were concentrated in the functions and pathways that could regulate the NSCs' behavior and the surrounding microenvironment.
evidence: Based on GO and KEGG pathway enrichment analysis results

claim: Inflammation and oxidative stress-related genes and signaling pathways were highly enriched in the target genes.
source: Interestingly, inflammation and oxidative stress-related genes and signaling pathways were also highly enriched in the target genes, consistent with the antioxidant role of exosomes as disclosed by our study.
evidence: Based on GO and KEGG pathway enrichment analysis results

claim: Male C57BL/6 mice were selected due to estrogen and progesterone have recognized neuroprotective effects.
source: Male C57BL/6 mice (age: 7–8 weeks, weight: 22–24 g) were selected due to estrogen and progesterone have recognized neuroprotective effects (Newton et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Newton et al., 2022

claim: A 55% decrease in the rCBF of the ipsilateral hemisphere, as compared to contralateral hemisphere, was considered the threshold for successful establishment of cerebral ischemia.
source: A 55% decrease in the rCBF of the ipsilateral hemisphere, as compared to contralateral hemisphere, was considered the threshold for successful establishment of cerebral ischemia.
evidence: Based on established experimental protocol for MCAO/R model
